summary: Defines YANG modules for configuring and operating IPv4-in-IPv6 softwire Border Relays and Customer Premises Equipment. They cover Lightweight 4over6, MAP-E, and MAP-T, which are address-plus-port mechanisms for IPv4 service over IPv6 networks.

eli5.summary: These give a standard way to set up and check the gear that lets old internet addresses work across a new-style network.

questions: what is the difference between map-e and map-t
how to configure lightweight 4over6 with yang
subtitle: YANG modules for configuring and monitoring IPv4-in-IPv6 softwire routers: lw4o6, MAP-E and MAP-T.

tldr.problem: Operators who give customers IPv4 service across an IPv6 network with Address plus Port softwires have no standard, machine-readable way to configure and monitor the Border Relays and Customer Edge devices involved.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8676 defines three YANG modules: ietf-softwire-ce, ietf-softwire-br and ietf-softwire-common. They cover Lightweight 4over6, MAP-E and MAP-T, and are used over NETCONF or RESTCONF for configuration, operational state and notifications.
tldr.outcome: One model structure covers all three mechanisms, chosen by a 'binding' or 'algorithm' choice. The RFC also warns that write access to these nodes is sensitive and that some read access can be misused to track host activity.

today: RFC 8676 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated. It relies on the tunnel type module from RFC 8675, and IANA assigned tunnel type 18, aplusp, for it.

sections.title: Scope and Purpose
sections.content:
The IETF Softwire Working Group developed several IPv4-in-IPv6 softwire mechanisms. RFC 8676 is a companion to those architecture documents. It focuses on provisioning the Address plus Port (A+P) functional elements: Border Routers (BRs) and Customer Edge (CE) devices, which RFC 7596 calls Customer Premises Equipment.

Three mechanisms are covered: Lightweight 4over6 (lw4o6, RFC 7596), Mapping of Address and Port with Encapsulation (MAP-E, RFC 7597) and Mapping of Address and Port using Translation (MAP-T, RFC 7599). They follow the A+P approach of RFC 6346. A YANG module for Dual-Stack Lite is in RFC 8513.

The modules are written in YANG (RFC 7950) and are used with NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF (RFC 8040) for configuration, operational state and notifications.
sections.eli5: Some providers let many homes share one old-style internet address. Special boxes at the home and at the provider make that work. This RFC says how to write down the settings for those boxes.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.content:
The RFC uses BR as a general term for softwire tunnel concentrators. That covers both MAP Border Routers (RFC 7597) and Lightweight 4over6 lwAFTRs (RFC 7596). The word "algorithm" means the mapping algorithm defined in RFC 7597.

A network element may run one or several instances of a softwire mechanism, each with its own configuration. The term algo-instance covers both MAP-E and MAP-T instances, while binding instances are used for lw4o6.

The modules adopt the Network Management Datastore Architecture (RFC 8342), and tree diagram symbols are those of RFC 8340.
sections.eli5: BR is the provider's big box that talks to many homes. CE is the little box in each home. An instance is one separate set of settings on a box.

sections.title: How the Modules Are Organized
sections.content:
There are two main modules and one shared module:

  • ietf-softwire-ce configures and monitors the CE. It is defined as an augment of the interface module (RFC 8343).
  • ietf-softwire-br configures and monitors the BR.
  • ietf-softwire-common holds groups of common functions imported into the other two.

Splitting by role (CE or BR) rather than by technology was chosen because it follows the intended function and existing implementation approaches more closely, according to a note in the RFC. Within the CE and BR modules, YANG feature statements show which mechanisms a given element supports. A ce-type (or br-type) choice picks binding or algo, and inside the algo-instances container a data-plane choice picks encapsulation or translation.

The CE entry is added to the interface list only if the tunnel type, from the module in RFC 8675, is set to aplusp.
sections.eli5: There is one settings sheet for the home box, one for the provider box, and one shared page of rules both can use.

sections.title: The CE and BR Data Models
sections.content:
On the CE, optional softwire-payload-mtu sets the IPv4 MTU for the softwire, and softwire-path-mru sets the maximum IPv6 softwire packet size that can be received. Both are needed only if the implementation cannot calculate them itself. For lw4o6, binding-ipv6info chooses which IPv6 address is the tunnel source and br-ipv6-addr gives the remote BR address.

For MAP, each algo-instance has an ea-len (the length of the Embedded-Address in the mapping rule), a rule-ipv6-prefix, a rule-ipv4-prefix and a forwarding flag. If forwarding is not set, the rule is a Basic Mapping Rule only and must not be used for forwarding. MAP-E adds the BR's br-ipv6-addr; MAP-T adds the Default Mapping Rule prefix, dmr-ipv6-prefix. An optional algo-versioning container records a version number and date for logging or data retention.

The BR for lw4o6 keeps a binding-table of binding-entry items. Each ties together the lwB4's IPv6 address or prefix, the allocated IPv4 address and a restricted port-set (psid-offset, psid-len, psid). A BR binding instance also has softwire-num-max, which must not be zero because that would disable the instance, enable-hairpinning and an icmp-policy for ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 errors. The read-only active-softwire-num reports how many softwires are currently provisioned.
sections.eli5: Each home box is told which provider box to talk to and which share of the public address it may use. The provider box keeps a list matching each home to its share.

sections.title: Statistics, Notifications and Related Modules
sections.content:
Both modules include read-only traffic counters for sent, received and dropped IPv4 and IPv6 packets and bytes, dropped IPv4 fragments, reassembled IPv6 fragments and ICMP errors generated. The BR adds hairpin counters and a discontinuity-time.

NETCONF notifications are included. The CE sends ce-binding-ipv6-addr-change if its binding IPv6 address changes for any reason. The BR sends events when a binding entry or MAP rule is added, modified or invalidated through added-entry, modified-entry and invalid-entry.

The softwire modules cover only softwire-specific settings. A complete CE may also need IPv6 and IPv4 routing configuration (RFC 8349), and NAT44 port-set (PSID) or stateless NAT46 prefix configuration (RFC 8512). The CE must already have minimal IPv6 configuration so the NETCONF client can reach it.
sections.eli5: The boxes keep score of how much traffic they handle and can send a message when something important changes, like a home getting a new address.

sections.title: Configuration Examples
sections.content:
Appendix A gives XML examples. In the lw4o6 BR binding-table example, one entry maps the lwB4 IPv6 address 2001:db8::1 to the IPv4 address 192.0.2.1 with a PSID of 52 (0x34) and PSID length 8, with BR address 2001:db8:1::2.

The MAP-E BR example configures a forwarding mapping rule with rule IPv6 prefix 2001:db8::/40, rule IPv4 prefix 192.0.2.0/24 and an EA-bit length of 16. A third example configures an lw4o6 CE. These use documentation addresses and show how the modules combine with the routing and NAT modules.
sections.eli5: The RFC includes sample settings sheets already filled in, so readers can see what a real one looks like.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modules are accessed over NETCONF or RESTCONF, with SSH and TLS as the mandatory-to-implement secure transports and NACM (RFC 8341) for access control. All writable (config true) nodes are considered sensitive. The RFC lists attacks possible by someone who can write to the BR or CE:

  • Pointing br-ipv6-addr on a CE at an illegitimate BR to intercept all of that CE's traffic, with severe privacy implications.
  • Setting the MTU low to increase fragmentation.
  • Disabling hairpinning to block CE-to-CE communication.
  • Setting softwire-num-max very high so that a misbehaving user can overload the BR with softwires.
  • Setting icmpv4-rate or icmpv6-rate low, which can disable ICMP handling.
  • Installing entries to cause a notification-driven DDoS.

Some readable data may also be sensitive. The binding table and the algorithm configuration can be misused to track host activity, so read access should be controlled.
sections.eli5: Whoever can change these settings can send a home's traffic to the wrong place or overload the provider's box. So only trusted people should be allowed to change them.
